verification.summary:
I checked all 15 findings against their primary sources and did not WebFetch any utah.edu page. Their main conclusions hold up. Verified: GSU and ECU found effects only on concrete tasks. The scaled nudges were null. DeVry is the precedent for graduate-outcome claims. RNL ranks content needs above outcomes. Mines and Georgia Tech publish outcomes with their methods. USU and College Scorecard don't allow a fair U-vs-USU comparison. The bias papers and the self-selected chatbot success numbers also check out.

Corrections:
(1) The Page & Gehlbach loan effects are +5.5 pp (accept loan), +6.3 (loan counseling) and +6.9 (Stafford), not "+6 to 7". The FAFSA-verification-hold effect (-3.0 pp) is only marginal (p<.10). The issue is Oct-Dec 2017, not Nov.
(2) The 89.5% RAG accuracy comes from a research prototype built on ChatGPT 3.5, not a production bot. The issue is Vol 27(4) (DOI indicates Oct 2024; PolyU lists Oct 2025). So "production bots are wrong 1 in 5 to 10" rests on UCLA's unexplained 82% alone. UCLA's gains are "since the pilot's launch", not "after the pilot".
(3) LAist does not say students stopped using the bots. Some students interviewed said they avoid them, while officials report thousands of chats a month. The $151k-$500k range covers the three districts that answered the survey; Santa Monica pays $57k.
(4) 34 CFR 668.74(c) says "employment opportunities", not "job opportunities". The 5th Circuit (Apr 2024) held the 2022 rule's misrepresentation standards (668.71-75) likely too vague and postponed the borrower-defense provisions. Whether the exact quoted text is enforceable is a question for counsel. The core point (representatives, employability, omissions) is in the text.
(5) NACAC's AI item A.1(e) is not new in 2026. The board approved it in May 2025 and published it in Aug 2025. The 2026 revision summary doesn't mention AI, vendors or disparagement, though all three quoted passages are in the 2026 PDF.
(6) ASU ECEE labels its employer list "Companies hiring our graduates", not a career-fair list. Its wage table is labeled O*NET.

Labeling: EAB, Keystone, RNL (with Halda and Modern Campus) and Hannon Hill are vendors. EAB's press release was listed as a "survey". EAB's "react negatively" finding is about messages from institutions that students perceive as AI-written. It is not about a clearly labeled AI assistant.

The FTC 'Luring Test' post returns 404 on ftc.gov today. I confirmed its text from the Wayback Machine (May 1, 2023, Michael Atleson). It names education as an area and says people should know whether they are talking to a machine. The current FTC may no longer stand behind it.

checks.claim: Mines 2024-25: NACE guidelines, 94% data collection, 87% positive outcomes, 1,372 BS grads, $84,000 average self-reported base (industry only, no bonuses), mechanical 355 grads $81,700, N/A when too few; outcomes page leads with positive outcomes and response rate
checks.note: All match the report. Caveats: non-responders and 'not looking' graduates are removed from the positive-outcomes rate, and the outcomes page shows a '95% Average Response Rate', not the report's 94%. Mechanical's positive-outcome rate is 84%.

checks.claim: Georgia Tech 2023-24: bachelor's median $84,000, average $88,587, 1,916 responses, 42% response rate, three weeks before/after graduation, 'does not represent all employers or positions'; Purdue self-reported, shown only at 7+
checks.note: All match. GT figures are an at-graduation snapshot. Purdue: 'All salary data are self-reported', shown only 'if there are 7 or more salaries reported'.

checks.claim: ASU Fulton: 86% employed/offer within six months, $78,000 median, 46% research/internships, unnamed rankings, no cohort or method; ASU ECEE shows O*NET wages and an employer list (some schools mix in career-fair employer lists); NACE knowledge-rate definition
checks.note: The ASU Fulton figures and gaps are confirmed: the rankings are 'Top 10 in the world for employer-student connections' and '#13 in the U.S.', with no source named. ECEE credits O*NET for its wages. Its 11-company list is labeled 'Companies hiring our graduates', not a career-fair list, and gives no source or method. No cited page shows a career-fair list passed off as hires; Mines labels its count as 'employers actively recruited'. The NACE knowledge-rate definition matches.

checks.claim: USU engineering's only salary figure is a graduate-student survey, mean $57,729, URL suggests 2014-15; College Scorecard (Oct 2026) earnings 1-7 years after completion from IRS W-2, same method, only federal-aid recipients
checks.note: USU: 'The mean salary for graduates who had secured employment was $57,729', with a survey link to school_grad_studies_survey_2014_15 (about 11 years old). Two searches found no USU undergraduate engineering outcomes page, but that does not prove none exists. Scorecard: W-2 plus Schedule SE earnings for Title IV recipients only. It excludes completers still enrolled or not working.

checks.claim: Zheng (arXiv Dec 2023; journal 2025): 'a significant disparity' in recommended majors across race, gender, SES, score percentile; Shailya et al. IJCNLP-AACL Findings 2025: 360 profiles, 25,000+ recommendations, three open models, 'often reinforce gender stereotypes'
checks.note: The Zheng quote matches. It is published in Information Technology and Management 26(4):625-636, Dec 2025, and tested an unspecified ChatGPT API model. Shailya et al. tested LLaMA-3.1-8B, Gemma-7B and Mistral-7B. Small open models are a weak proxy for Haiku 5.5.

checks.claim: Lehigh quiz rates subject enjoyment and says it 'is not meant to be taken as concrete advice'; Illinois Grainger quiz says it 'can't make decisions for you' and points to an advisor
checks.note: Lehigh's quiz rates both enjoyment and skill in seven areas. The source text says 'concrete advise' (sic). Illinois quote and advisor referral confirmed.

checks.claim: Illinois Gies (Juji, 2022): '72% more likely to apply', initial and self-selected; USC Aiken (AdmitHub, 2019): '28 percent more students have committed', no control
checks.note: Gies: 'Initial data has shown that prospective students who interacted with Alma were 72% more like [sic] to apply'. This was for an online MBA, a graduate program. USC Aiken: fall 2019 vs fall 2018, from 'a news announcement', with no control group. Both are older than 2023 and self-reported by the schools.

skipped: Anything on the utah.edu side: whether the U is a NACAC member, whether U pages already offer a U-vs-USU salary comparison, and what U outcomes data exist. The ground rules don't allow fetching utah.edu.
Whether the FTC's jurisdiction over public universities is limited (this is the other researcher's commentary, not in the cited source).

Whether the 2022 amendments to 34 CFR 668.71-75 are currently in force after the CCST v. ED litigation. I read only the Apr 2024 5th Circuit opinion, not later district-court orders or the 2025 Supreme Court docket.
Whether USU has any other engineering salary page beyond the graduate-programs page. I ran two web searches, which can't prove a negative.

research.summary:
utah.edu can support a recruiting voice built on concrete, dated facts. It can't yet support the "salaries by major" centerpiece of the take-home PDF.

Solid today:
- The 2026-27 cost of attendance (resident $45,878 on campus; tuition and fees $10,480 resident, $32,932 non-resident, $15,720 WUE), the engineering differential ($71.21 per credit hour), and WUE rules.
- The U's self-description as "Lowest Tuition Among AAU Public Universities in the West" (about.utah.edu).
- Scholarships: "up to 290 scholarships" through one PCE application (not 300); civil pages say PCE awarded $2,800,000 across 700 scholarships.
- Hands-on work: industry-sponsored capstone, the ECE Engineering Clinic, CS clinical capstone, competition teams, UROP ($1,200 per semester), ChE ">30% of undergraduates" in research, and the Ambassadors.
- Career infrastructure: STEM Internship and Career Fair on Jan 25, 2027; U Career Success had 19,884 coaching appointments and ran 26 career fairs from May 2025 to April 2026.
- Distinctive firsts: first AI bachelor's in Utah, the only materials science and engineering program in Utah, U.S. News 2026 Nuclear Engineering #26, Game/Simulation Development #2, undergraduate entrepreneurship #8.
- College scale: a record 1,298 degrees in 2025, 218 tenure-track faculty, more than $91M research funding.

Weak:
- Per-major starting salaries exist only for mechanical (BS $64,488; page last edited 2023, no class year or sample size), MSE/MetE (a round $60,000), and civil (93% employed; no salary). The EE figure ($70,000, 99% employment) is stale.
- BME, ChE, CS and computer engineering have no U salary figures at all.
- The U runs a NACE First-Destination Survey, but we found no public by-major report on careers.utah.edu.
- Overall rankings are middling and falling (graduate engineering 65th in the 2026 edition, down from 55th in 2024), so leading with them backfires.

College Scorecard has U-vs-USU median earnings by major (federal data, Title IV recipients only). Using it needs a rule change. Its results are mixed: the U is higher in mechanical and electrical engineering, USU is higher in civil one year out.

Several department pages a recruiting answer would draw on are stale or contradict each other: "Most affordable Pac-12" while other U pages say the U is in the Big 12, an undated BME rank of 38th, and conflicting scholarship counts and deadlines. A recruiting-tuned bot would repeat these.

Best path: ask the college or U Career Success to publish the engineering FDS breakdown by major on a utah.edu page, index it plus about.utah.edu, data.utah.edu, the 2026 rankings article and the cost-of-attendance page, and fix the stale pages first.

facts.fact: Average Starting Salary (ME BS): $64,488; (ME MS): $79,388; (ME PhD): $95,965. "Based on the information gathered by University of Utah's Career Services": 68.3% have secured a post graduation position before graduation; Average Salary: $71,253; Employed in Utah: 71.3%.
facts.as_of: page last modified 2023-09-28; no class year
facts.caveats: No class year, sample size, response rate or method. 'Average Salary $71,253' is not defined: BS only, or all degrees? This is the only per-major salary from Career Services on any college site.

facts.fact: Career Outlook (both MSE and Metallurgical): "Approximately 50% of our undergraduates receive offers of employment before graduating, with an average salary of $60,000."
facts.caveats: Round number with no year, n or source. '50% before graduating' could read as a negative in a recruiting context.

facts.fact: "The average starting salary for students graduating with a bachelor's degree in Metallurgical Engineering is approximately $60,000/yr. Job placement for metallurgical engineers is typically near 100%."
facts.caveats: No source or year for the salary. Its 'near 100%' placement sits uneasily with the prospective page's '~50% receive offers before graduating'.

facts.fact: "93% employment rate upon graduation" / "93% of our students have job offers upon graduation"; "$111,000 in scholarships Awarded".
facts.caveats: No class year, n or method. No salary given for civil.

facts.fact: "Electrical engineers are in great demand, and our graduates have a starting salary average of $70,000and 99% employment."
facts.as_of: page modified 2024-12-13; text is an old Engineering Day session blurb (same page mentions 'the March 18th earthquake')
facts.caveats: Undated, no source; likely several years old. Don't use as a current figure.

facts.fact: "Electrical Engineers: average salary of $75,300"; "Computer Hardware Engineers: average salary of $87,700"; "national mean annual salary that is on average $12,000 higher"; "Top 20% salary for EE $151,700; CE $185,200".
facts.caveats: National occupation figures, not U graduates; no source year. A bot could easily present these as 'U grads earn'.

facts.fact: Gardner Institute report (as summarized by the college): "Utahns with engineering jobs made an average of $96,600 in wages in 2020, and computer science workers earned $89,500—80% and 66% higher than the $53,800 state average"; graduates employed in Utah "earn 31% more after four years and 59% more after eight years"; "In 2020, the University of Utah had the highest number of engineering degrees in the state at 805 completions, representing 41% of the USHE total. Utah State followed with 497 (25%)." U had 571 CS completions (32%).
facts.caveats: Statewide wages, not U-graduate wages. Data from 2020. The full report (gardner.utah.edu/wp-content/uploads/ECS-Report-Oct2022.pdf) redirects to CloudFront and was not read. This is the only utah.edu page comparing the U to USU, and only on degree counts.

facts.fact: U Career Success formally launched summer 2023; "In its first year alone, the undergraduate career outcome rate increased nearly 10%, according to data from the First-Destination Survey." From May 2025 to April 2026: 19,884 career-coaching appointments (vs 17,891 the previous year); 26 career fairs, 243 career workshops and 242 employer events.
facts.caveats: Confirms the U runs a NACE-standard First-Destination Survey, but no rate, salary or by-college breakdown is published. careers.utah.edu's homepage, employers and events pages contain none. The 'Where Are They Now?' URLs from search (careers.utah.edu/?p=263, /where-are-they-now/) returned 404.

facts.fact: "Who Hires Our Graduates?": Amazon, Apple, Google, Hill Air Force Base, Intel Corp, L3Harris, LightSmyth Technologies, Macom, Micron, Microsoft, Northrup Grumman, Nvidia, Pacificorp, Raytheon, Rocky Mountain Power, Sandia National Labs, TD Williamson, Zeiss. Quote: "We would hire every graduating senior from the University of Utah if they applied" (unattributed).
facts.caveats: Undated list; misspelling 'Northrup'. The quote has no attribution and shouldn't be repeated.

facts.fact: "Companies hiring recent graduates include Micron Technology, Teva Pharmaceuticals, Proctor & Gamble, Halliburton, Rio Tinto, Archer Daniels Midland, Nestlé, L-3 Communications, Celanese, ICU Medical, FLSmidth, Aecom." Also: "More than 30% of our undergraduates are involved in research in professors' labs"; "vibrant cooperative education program".
facts.caveats: A different list is on che.utah.edu/prospective/ (2025-06-03): Boeing, Merck, Weider Nutrition Group, Halliburton, General Electric, Bechtel, Weyerhauser, EPA, Huntsman Chemical, Cargill, Myriad Genetics. Neither list is dated.

facts.fact: MSE grads went to Intel, USSynthetic, Fisher Company, Northrop Grumman, Stryker, IM Flash. MetE grads went to Intel, General Electric, ArcelorMittal, Carpenter Alloys, Newmont, Rio Tinto, Freeport McMoRan Inc, Department of Energy, Space X ("the past couple of years").
facts.caveats: 'Past couple of years' is undated. ME publishes job titles only, plus a LinkedIn alumni search link. BME and CS publish no employer list.

facts.fact: "With nearly 1,400 engineering and computer science graduates each year... Our 200+ engineering faculty members in seven academic departments"; "The University of Utah Career Services Center hosts an Engineering and Science Job Fair in the fall and a university-wide Job Fair in the spring"; senior projects and clinics with industry mentors.
facts.caveats: Fair names and timing conflict with careers.utah.edu, which lists a 'STEM Internship and Career Fair' on January 25, 2027 and no fall engineering fair.

facts.fact: STEM Internship and Career Fair: January 25, 2027, 9 am - 3 pm, A. Ray Olpin Student Union, Ballroom. Biomedical & Health Sciences Career Panel & Networking Event: November 17, 2026, 12:30-3:30 pm, Eccles Health Sciences Education Building.
facts.caveats: Changes every semester. Good for a 'next step' in recruiting answers if the page is indexed. careers.utah.edu/employers/ lists a relationship manager for 'Engineering, Energy & Defense' and one for 'Technology'.

facts.fact: "Every semester the career center puts on a STEM Career & Internship Fair. Over 100 employers come to recruit students for internships and full-time jobs." Handshake connects students with "more than 250,000 employers, including all Fortune 500 companies."
facts.caveats: The Handshake figure is the vendor's claim from its launch. The page uses the old office name 'Career and Professional Development Center'.

facts.fact: Internship/co-op for credit: ECE 3990 Co-op, ME EN 5910 Co-op, CS 4010 CS Internship, ChE Cooperative Education (1+ credit/semester for 20+ hrs/week), BME Industrial Co-op and Internship Program.
facts.caveats: No participation rates published.

facts.fact: Strategic partnerships: Sandia National Laboratories MOU (students and faculty can work for set periods in Sandia facilities); DOE National Laboratory of the Rockies MOU signed May 4, 2026; Idaho National Laboratory partnership (Feb 2022) and U.S. Air Force/Hill AFB education partnership (Nov 2022).
facts.caveats: These are research MOUs, not hiring commitments. Phrase as 'opportunities', not jobs.

facts.fact: 2026-2027 Cost of Attendance, undergraduate, living on campus: Tuition & Fees $10,480 resident / $32,932 non-resident / $15,720 WUE; Housing $11,300; Food $7,898; Total of Direct and Indirect Costs $45,878 / $68,330 / $51,118.
facts.caveats: University-wide estimate. Doesn't include the engineering differential. Off-campus and with-parent totals differ.

facts.fact: 2026-27 lower division, resident, 15 credit hours: Total Tuition & Fees $5,582.96 per semester. "Engineering Undergraduate Courses: All students... will be charged an additional $71.21 per credit hour for undergraduate courses (1000-5999 level courses) in the College of Engineering."
facts.caveats: There is no annual 'engineering cost' figure. Any per-year differential would be our arithmetic and should say so.

facts.fact: WUE: "the recipient pays no more than 150% of the standard resident tuition rate" (excludes differential and fees, up to 18 hours). For 2026-27 freshmen: application complete by December 1, 2025; unweighted GPA 3.30+; renewable up to 8 semesters with 3.00 GPA and 24 credits/year. Recipients "generally cannot receive any other university merit award".
facts.caveats: Freshman scholarship page (live) says eligibility for Fall 2027 is now set by the Office of Admissions. The indexed WUE page covers Fall 2026 entrants only.

facts.fact: "Lowest Tuition Among AAU Public Universities in the West"; "85% U Students Receive Financial Support"; "82% of degrees awarded are in programs related to high-demand jobs"; "600+ student organizations"; "$781M Research Funding in FY25"; "#8 Undergrad Entrepreneur Program (U.S. News 2026)"; "Since 2000, the U has launched 360+ companies"; "515 student startup teams launched in 2025"; Tier 1 research university, AAU member.
facts.caveats: This is the U's own comparative claim, so it's citable. 'Lowest tuition among AAU publics in the West' is the cleanest 'better without saying it' cost line. Note the 85% vs 87% aid conflict with admissions.utah.edu/financial-aid-scholarships/.

facts.fact: "Most Price College of Engineering (PCE) scholarships are now routed through a single application: 'PCE General Scholarships'. Through this application, you will be reviewed for up to 290 scholarships across the college and departments." Incoming freshmen who apply to the U by December 1st are automatically considered for PCE merit scholarships (transfers by February 1st), but must select an engineering major on the admissions application. PCE loans: $1,000 to $10,000 per year, lifetime max $20,000, 5% interest.
facts.caveats: The notes say '300 available'; the page says 'up to 290' and that's the number to use. The same page contradicts itself on deadlines (February 1 vs February 8; references due 'January' vs 'February 7th'). No award amounts or averages are given.

facts.fact: "The John and Marcia Price College of Engineering has awarded $2,800,000 in scholarships. With 900 applications received and 700 scholarships awarded, students have access to significant financial support."
facts.as_of: page modified 2026-10-12; award year not stated
facts.caveats: Undated. Conflicts with 'up to 290 scholarships' (price.utah.edu/scholarships) and 'More than 480 scholarships are awarded each year' (price.utah.edu/support/scholarship-campaign, 2023). Dept figures: ChE 'more than $100,000' annually (price.utah.edu/enroll), ECE '70 scholarships and fellowships' last year (ece.utah.edu/chairs-message/, 2026-05-06).

facts.fact: University merit scholarships for Fall 2027 freshmen: complete admissions application by December 1, 2026; notifications begin January 18, 2027; FAFSA priority February 1. Listed awards: President John R. Park, Provost's, Bonneville, Red Rock, Great Salt Lake, Lone Star, Alumni Legacy, Sterling Scholars Tuition Waiver. "Students from a WUE state or territory are not eligible to be considered for the above listed merit scholarships."
facts.caveats: Amounts are behind 'View Requirements' and were not read.

facts.fact: "In 2025, the Price College of Engineering once again set an annual record for the number of engineering degrees it has awarded: 1298"; "218 tenure-track faculty members"; "more than $91 million in engineering-related research funding in 2025 (including sub-awards)". ASEE Profiles ranks: 36th in engineering doctoral degrees, 33rd in tenured/tenure-track faculty, 36th in undergraduate enrollment, 30th in CS bachelor's, 46th in ChE bachelor's.
facts.as_of: page modified 2026-08-25; ASEE year not stated ('latest statistics')
facts.caveats: '$91M' conflicts with the 2023 post's 'more than $100 million in annual research expenditures', probably a different measure. The ASEE ranks measure size, not quality.

facts.fact: ME Capstone Senior Design: two semesters, project "defined and funded by an industry sponsor", teams of 4 to 6, approx. 9 hours/student/week. Sheldon X. Wang & April M. Xie Senior Design Lab: 3,500 sq ft with FDM and resin 3D printers, large laser cutter, CNC plasma cutter, welding. Design Day: Fall 2026 December 8th; Spring 2027 April 22nd.
facts.caveats: Also: ECE Engineering Clinic Program, industry-sponsored capstones for computer, electrical and mechanical (ece.utah.edu/senior-capstone-experience/the-engineering-clinic-program/). CS Clinical Capstone 'sponsored by local industry' (cs.utah.edu/undergraduate/academic-programs/senior-capstone/).

facts.fact: Competition teams: Aerospace Club (Spaceport America rocket competition), Formula SAE (Formula U Racing), ASME/IEEE Heat Sink Challenge, Utah Student Robotics (NASA Lunabotics), Fluid Power Vehicle Challenge, Baja SAE. Also: "Students compete in at least one mechanical-engineering related competition every year" (price.utah.edu/enroll).
facts.caveats: No recent results or awards on the college sites (competition news posts are 2011-2015).

facts.fact: UROP "Funding ($1200/semester for up to 2 semesters...)"; any research with any faculty can count toward technical electives (ECE 3970). ME UROP Fall 2026 lists 16 student awardees with faculty mentors.
facts.caveats: price.utah.edu/student-research (2023-07-03) says 'up to $1200 for any first-time UROP student' and lists 2023 REU deadlines, so it's stale.

facts.fact: PCE Ambassadors "serve as the official student representatives and Recognized Student Government"; they lead engineering campus tours, support outreach and recruitment events, and serve on one of four committees. "Submit your question below, and a PCE Ambassador will get back to you" (Ask an Ambassador).
facts.caveats: Ask an Ambassador is a natural human handoff for recruiting conversations.

facts.fact: U.S. News 2026: Best Engineering Schools 65; Biomedical 46; Chemical 67; Civil 68; Computer Engineering 50; Electrical 52; Materials 58; Mechanical 60; Nuclear Engineering 26; Computer Science 46; Undergrad Engineering Programs 64; Undergrad Computer Science Programs 63; Game/Simulation Development 2; Entrepreneurship (undergrad) 8; National Universities 151; Top Public Schools 79.
facts.caveats: Graduate engineering fell from 55th (2024 edition, per price.utah.edu/2023/04/25/pcoe-goes-up-in-rankings) to 65th. Most numbers are mid-pack, so highlight only the standouts (Nuclear 26, Game/Sim 2, Entrepreneurship 8). Re-index each year.

facts.fact: "The University of Utah is the highest-ranked public college in the West and Stanford University is the region's top private school, according to the Wall Street Journal/College Pulse 2024 Best Colleges in the U.S. ranking."
facts.caveats: Two editions old. We didn't check for a newer WSJ result.

facts.fact: 38,261 credit-taking students enrolled for 2025-2026 (fall census); "19 to 1" student-to-faculty ratio; 86% retention (Fall 2024 to Fall 2025); 1,721 tenure-line faculty (2025); $789M HERD research expenditures; $1.6B endowment.
facts.caveats: obia.utah.edu now redirects here (UAIR). Its dashboards page is JavaScript-rendered and returned no text. Conflicts: admissions.utah.edu says '18:1'. $789M (HERD) vs $781M FY25 on about.utah.edu are different measures.

facts.fact: Fall 2024: record incoming class of 6,001 ("nearly 34% increase from the incoming class of 2020"); total enrollment 36,881, "its highest level in the U's 174-year history"; fifth straight record year.
facts.caveats: University-wide. The newest college-level enrollment we found is 2023 (5,244 undergraduates, price.utah.edu/2023/04/25/pcoe-goes-up-in-rankings).

facts.fact: Bachelor's in Artificial Intelligence "is the first of its kind in the state of Utah, and will begin accepting applicants for the Fall 2026 semester"; "In 1964, we were one of the first programs in the nation to offer a BS in Computer Science." Also: MSE is "The only materials science and engineering program in Utah"; Civil is "One-of the few civil and environmental engineering departments in the country with a program in nuclear engineering" (price.utah.edu/enroll).
facts.caveats: These are the U's own 'only/first' claims, so they're citable. That makes them the best material for 'better without saying better'.

facts.fact: "In 2024, Utah took the top overall spot for the second year running" (U.S. News Best States); "#1 Employment", "#2 Education", "#3 Economy"; Utah "one of the fastest-growing tech sectors in the country".
facts.caveats: Many other location rankings on ece.utah.edu/life-in-utah (2020) and price.utah.edu/enroll carry no year, so treat those as stale.

facts.fact: College Scorecard median earnings 1 year after a bachelor's (n = working, not enrolled). University of Utah: Computer Science (CIP 1107) $96,677 (n 181); Computer Engineering $87,804 (24); Electrical $83,204 (56); Mechanical $78,453 (163); Civil $76,561 (49); Biomedical $74,614 (58); Chemical $73,651 (43); Materials $71,658 (23). Utah State: Mechanical $72,131 (158); Civil $78,316 (57); Electrical $76,257 (43); Computer & Info Sciences General (CIP 1101) $76,555 (142).
facts.as_of: API 'latest' fields pulled 2026-11-04; Field of Study documentation version October 2026
facts.caveats: Not utah.edu, so using it needs a rule change. Title IV aid recipients only, W-2 earnings, inflation-adjusted, pooled two-year cohorts. Exact cohort years not resolved. Small n for several majors. CS CIP codes differ between schools. Mixed result: the U is higher for ME and EE, USU is higher for civil at 1 year.

stale_content.what: 'National starting salary for mechanical engineering graduating seniors: $64,000' (2013 NACE via WSJ). Ranks #1 in local search for 'starting salary', so the bot will surface it.
Kiplinger 'top 5 majors' salary claim. Related old posts: mech.utah.edu/top-jobs-2013-mechanical-engineer/ (2013), mech.utah.edu/best-paying-for-women/ (2012).

'Most affordable Pac-12 institution', but the U's own pages say it is now Big 12 (civil.utah.edu/about/, mech.utah.edu/department/about-mechanical-engineering/living-in-salt-lake/). Also 'recently ranked 35-40 by the Academic Ranking of World Universities' links to a 2017 post.

'Most affordable Pac-12 institution'; undated national salary figures that read like U-grad salaries; 'nearly 50 individuals scholarships each year totaling over $200,000' (the ECE chair's 2026 message says 70); undated 'Why Utah' rankings.

BME 'Ranked 38th (out of 129 schools) by U.S. News' with no year (2026 U.S. News BME is 46). ECE '31-percent increase in research spending since 2013' and '95-percent increase in faculty since 2006'. EAE 'No. 1-ranked' (Princeton Review) with no year. Utah and SLC rankings with no years.
EE 'starting salary average of $70,000 and 99% employment', undated text from an old Engineering Day session.
Graduate engineering 55th in the 2024 U.S. News edition; it's 65th in the 2026 edition. College stats '5,244 undergraduate students... 214 tenure-track faculty' are from 2023.
Contradicts itself: February 1 vs February 8 deadlines, and references due 'January' vs 'February 7th'. 'List of Scholarships Coming Soon!'
'More than 480 scholarships are awarded each year', which conflicts with 'up to 290' (scholarships page) and '700 scholarships awarded' (civil pages).
Promotes the '2026 U of U STEM Career Fair' with 'Tuesday, September 10th' sessions and location 'TBD'. In 2026, September 10 is a Thursday, so these look like old dates.

'Engineering and Science Job Fair in the fall and a university-wide Job Fair in the spring' and 'Career Services Center'. careers.utah.edu (U Career Success) now lists a 'STEM Internship and Career Fair' on Jan 25, 2027.
Uses the old 'Career and Professional Development Center' name and says Handshake is a newly launched system. The office is now U Career Success (price.utah.edu/career-coaching).
2023 TREU REU deadlines ('April 15, 2023'). 'one of 65 members' of AAU.
Points students to the '2022-2023 Academic Year Cost of Attendance' (current: 2026-2027).
'The University of Utah is number one in the nation in producing start-up companies', with no year or source. The only support in the index is a 2010 post (mech.utah.edu/u-of-u-no-1-for-startups/).
'Placement Rate for Graduates Exceeds 90%' is a national AIMBE survey item.

Not in our index, but the stats are stale: 'Top 50 Ranked Among the Nation's Public Universities (US News & World Report, 2023-2024)' (2026 is 79th Top Public) and '$686M Research Funding Received in Fiscal Year 2022' (about.utah.edu says $781M FY25). Its '18:1' conflicts with data.utah.edu '19 to 1'.
Says the Price Computing and Engineering Building 'will open in 2026'. Nothing in the index confirms it opened.

third_party_sources.name: College Scorecard, Field of Study data (U.S. Dept. of Education)
third_party_sources.what: Median earnings 1, 4, 5 and 7 years after completion by institution and 4-digit CIP field. Lets us compare the U and USU major by major. The API takes DEMO_KEY (U id 230764, USU 230728). Spot-check pulled 2026-11-04: U ME $78,453 vs USU $72,131 at 1 year.
third_party_sources.caveats: Federal, not utah.edu, so it breaks the grounding rule unless the rule changes. Title IV aid recipients only ('should not assume that Scorecard data values are representative of all students'); working-and-not-enrolled only; W-2 earnings, inflation-adjusted; pooled cohorts that are several years old. Counts are perturbed and many U majors are suppressed or small (n 23-58). CIP codes don't line up across schools (U CS 1107 vs USU 1101). Results are mixed: USU civil is higher at 1 year.

third_party_sources.name: NACE Winter 2026 Salary Survey
third_party_sources.what: National projected starting salary for Class of 2026 engineering bachelor's: $81,198 (up 3.1% from $78,731).
third_party_sources.caveats: Employer projections from 150 respondents (20.3% response rate), surveyed Oct 8 - Nov 30, 2025. National, not U-specific, base salary only. The full report is paid (NACE is a membership association that sells it). The U's First-Destination Survey uses NACE's standard.

third_party_sources.name: USHE Graduate Workforce Outcomes dashboard
third_party_sources.what: 'Analyze workforce outcomes for graduates, including employment, salaries, and industry placement following completion.' The page links 'ROI of USHE Awards' and 'High-Yield Graduates'. A USHE 2024 agenda (ushe.edu/wp-content/uploads/pdf/agendas/2024/202408/Program_Workforce_Evaluation.pdf, from search, not opened) describes institution-by-program views with placement rate and median salary.
third_party_sources.caveats: The dashboard is interactive and its text wasn't readable. We couldn't confirm the filters, data years, or whether wages are Utah-only. research.summary: The U's brand and accessibility rules point to one design. Build the take-home as an accessible, branded HTML summary page. Open it from the widget in a new tab, lay it out for phones first, and give it a print stylesheet so it also prints as one page. A real PDF file comes second, generated from the same template. That route also gives the most visual result, because phones show web pages better than PDFs. The 2024 DOJ Title II rule requires WCAG 2.1 AA for the U's web content, including PDFs. The April 2026 interim final rule moved the U's compliance date to April 26, 2027 without changing what is required. The U's own pages call that 'not a stop-work order' and say to prefer web pages over documents. Image-based infographics fail WCAG 1.4.5 (html2canvas, PNG exports). So do browser-printed PDFs from iPhones: WebKit gives no outline and I found no evidence it tags them, and about 87% of US teens own an iPhone. Brand rules are strict and approval-gated. Use only official logo files, which need a uNID to download. Never build a hybrid mark with the assistant's name. Get the Price College lockup from college communications. Under Policy 3-163, a student's use of U trademarks needs pre-approval from the Trademarks and Licensing Office, unless the college is the publisher of record. The fonts are Myriad Pro and Factoria, and the U approves no substitutes. But the Adobe Fonts terms forbid self-hosting the font files, so a server-side PDF renderer cannot legally use them without a separate license. Three content constraints follow. UMC's AI guidelines expect a human to review AI-made material and discourage AI-made whole pieces or images, so use a fixed template approved once, filled from a vetted fact table. The brand's 'Collaborative' pillar argues against a U-vs-Utah State chart on U-branded paper. The vendor surveys (RNL, EAB) say students want majors, scholarships and cost, and parents want hands-on learning, job placement and earnings. Students also prefer choosing what they see over automatic personalization, so let them pick the sections. Process note: I read 34 utah.edu URLs through the polite helper, over the suggested 25, and a few of them were 404 or login redirects. The 10-second per-host spacing held throughout.

findings.claim: Logo use is locked down: use only official files, never alter or combine them, and college lockups come only from UMC's approved secondary-logo system.
findings.evidence: brand.utah.edu Logos & Marks: a uNID is required to download brand assets. The primary logo may not be smaller than 100 px wide on the web, and the horizontal logo not smaller than 150 px. Clear space is 1/4 the height of the Block U. The prohibited list includes: do not use the logo as a background or watermark, do not place it on backgrounds that fail accessibility standards, and do not incorporate the logo into another logo, lockup, or hybrid mark. Secondary logos for colleges have four parts: the Block U, the wordmark, the signature in Myriad Pro Bold, and a red ruled line. 'These are the only approved logo applications... No designs... that differ... should be created or used.' They are requested through a uNID-gated form. The Block U suits in-state audiences and the Interlocking U suits national ones, but the Interlocking U must not be substituted on secondary logos.
findings.implication: Put the official Price College secondary logo file, supplied by college communications, in the header at 150 px or larger with clear space. Do not draw the lockup in CSS or SVG, and do not pair the U logo with a 'Price Engineering Assistant' mark. Keep the logo on a plain white or red field, never over a photo or watermark.

findings.claim: A student using U trademarks needs pre-approval from the Trademarks and Licensing Office. Institutional web pages have fixed header and footer requirements.
findings.evidence: Policy 3-163 (effective April 9, 2024): 'Students and student groups are permitted to use University Trademarks with permission from the Trademarks and Licensing Office... must be pre-approved.' Departments' marketing use 'shall comply with the Brand Standards' and with Rule 4-003G. Rule 4-003G: institutional sites need a UMC-approved logo in the upper left linking to utah.edu, plus footer links to utah.edu/disclaimer, utah.edu/privacy and utah.edu/nondiscrimination. On non-institutional sites, logo use other than by faculty or staff needs approval from the University Licensing Manager.

sources.title: Rule 4-003G Web Site and Web Page Design Requirements

findings.implication: Settle who publishes the take-home before adding any logo. If the college is the publisher, its communications office approves the template. If it is the student project, Trademarks and Licensing must pre-approve it. Either way, the page footer should carry the disclaimer, privacy and nondiscrimination links.

findings.claim: Colors: Utah Red must lead, the core palette is red, black, white and Zion Cinder Cone, and accents are capped at 10% and kept away from logos. Charts may use accents, but on white only the core colors and Granite Peak meet WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: brand.utah.edu Colors: core colors are Utah Red #BE0000, black, white and Zion Cinder Cone #707271. Utah Red 'must be prioritized' and must feature 'as the leading brand color.' Accent colors are 'allowed only in a clearly limited and secondary role.' They may be used for 'data visualizations (e.g., charts, graphs, or infographics),' may not be used with logos, and 'may not exceed 10% of the overall design.' I computed contrast ratios against white: Utah Red 6.58, Zion Cinder Cone 4.85, Granite Peak 3.49, Mountain Green 2.22, Great Salt Lake 2.24, Wasatch Sunrise 1.73, Salt Flat Grey 1.26. Red against black is 3.19. The brand accessibility page lists the approved text pairings, for example Utah Red on white or Salt Flat Grey, and Wasatch Sunrise only with black or Red Rocks.
findings.implication: Draw charts on white with Utah Red, black and Zion Cinder Cone, adding Granite Peak only if needed. Bright accents fall below the 3:1 non-text contrast on white, so use them only as small details with black text on top. Label values directly so meaning never depends on color alone.

findings.claim: The published color specs disagree with each other in places, and an older toolkit advises against blue or purple.
findings.evidence: On the current Colors page, Red Rocks is listed as RGB 130-0-0 (which is #820000) but HEX #890000. The October 2023 color toolkit PDF lists Zion Cinder Cone as an accent, PMS 403, #8D857E. The current page lists it as a core color, PMS 424, #707271. The toolkit also says it is 'strongly recommended that designers avoid using blue or purple as stand-alone colors to avoid creating confusion with other regional universities' school colors.' The current page does not repeat that line.

sources.title: University of Utah brand colors toolkit (2023 PDF)

findings.implication: Use the current web page's values, which the widget already uses: #890000 and #707271. Ask UMC to confirm the Red Rocks value. Avoid blue, especially in any chart that names another school; Utah State's color is blue.

findings.claim: The brand fonts are Myriad Pro and Factoria with no approved substitutes. The Adobe Fonts terms allow them on websites but forbid self-hosting, so a server-side PDF renderer cannot use them.
findings.evidence: brand.utah.edu Typography: Myriad Pro is the primary body face, Factoria is for headlines and should be used 'sparingly,' and Kepler and Industry are secondary. Trajan Pro 3 is reserved for the wordmark. 'The University of Utah does not approve the use of substitute fonts.' Yet the page's 'Download Font from Adobe Fonts' link points to Source Sans 3 on Google Fonts. Adobe Fonts Additional Terms (effective April 16, 2020; a newer version may exist): web fonts may be used 'to design and develop your Websites' through a Web Project. Embedding desktop fonts into a Document 'for printing and viewing' is allowed if the font is subset. Prohibited: 'hosting the Licensed Content on your own server' and copying fonts out of a Web Project. The widget already accepts data-adobe-fonts and otherwise falls back to Open Sans, Work Sans and Poppins.
findings.implication: Rendering in the browser with the U's Adobe Fonts project is on-brand and licensed. A WeasyPrint or Playwright PDF on Cloud Run would need an open font such as Source Sans 3 (OFL) unless UMC has a server license. Ask UMC whether Source Sans 3 is an acceptable fallback, since its own page links to it.

findings.claim: The brand's own voice argues against direct rival comparisons. It also gives vetted 'U facts' copy and a storytelling checklist the take-home can use.
findings.evidence: The Collaborative pillar: 'We are poised, confident leaders who embrace competing ideas and institutions. Rather than feeling threatened, we uplift...' and 'We're community-centered, not self-focused.' The Confident pillar calls for 'strong, active language' and an 'optimistic and forward-looking tone.' The Storytelling Mandatories ask every story to use at least three of these: broader impact, collaboration, 'the majesty of the place,' authentic voices, 'compelling visuals... infographics,' and others. The UMC boilerplates are a 'vetted description of the U' for 'marketing or PR collateral.' Examples: flagship institution, 18 schools and colleges, more than 100 majors, more than 38,000 students, AAU member (71 institutions), and a record $781 million in FY25 sponsored research.
findings.implication: 'Better without saying it' fits the brand if the sheet shows the U's own outcomes in confident language and leaves out a U-vs-Utah State chart. Take the 'U facts' block from the boilerplate verbatim, with its date, and re-check it each year. Use place, hands-on experience and a real student voice from a utah.edu page to meet the storytelling mandatories.

findings.claim: UMC's AI guidelines expect a human to review all AI-made material, call for transparency, and steer away from AI-made whole pieces or images. They exclude chatbots, but a branded take-home is close to marketing collateral.
findings.evidence: The guidelines apply to 'communications and marketing professionals' and are 'not intended to govern... chatbots.' They say: 'All AI generated material must be carefully reviewed, approved, edited and overseen by a human author.' Also 'We commit to verifying the accuracy of information supplied by AI' and 'transparency in AI usage is essential.' @theU (January 9, 2024): the guidelines 'advise employees not to use generative AI tools to create entire pieces of content or images.' The working group then included Evan Lerner, director of communications, College of Engineering.

sources.title: New AI guidelines for U marketing and communications (@theU, 2024)

findings.implication: Don't let the model write the branded sheet freely. Use a template approved once by college communications, with numbers, salaries and U facts drawn from a dated, human-checked fact table. The model only chooses modules and writes a short summary labeled as AI-written. Use no AI-made images. The college's communications director is the natural reviewer (confirm the current person).

findings.claim: There is no public infographic or one-pager template. Presentation templates, letterhead, photo-permission guidance and logo files are behind uNID login, and UMC offers design help through a request form.
findings.evidence: The Permission Guidelines for Photos/Videos and Presentation Templates pages redirected to CAS login (go.utah.edu), and Letterhead is under /secure/. The Contact page says to submit 'project details, and an account executive will reach out... walk you through our creative brief.' Logo pages say 'A uNID is required to download University Brand Assets.'
findings.implication: Ask college communications (or UMC through the form) for an existing one-pager or fact-sheet template and for photos cleared for use. I could not read the photo-permission rules, so leave photos of identifiable people out until they confirm.

findings.claim: The DOJ ADA Title II rule requires WCAG 2.1 AA for the U's web content and PDFs, and the U's deadline is now April 26, 2027. The requirements did not change.
findings.evidence: 28 CFR 35.200(b)(1): beginning April 26, 2027, an entity with a population of 50,000 or more must ensure that web content it provides 'directly or through contractual, licensing, or other arrangements' complies with WCAG 2.1 Level A and AA. Section 35.104 defines conventional electronic documents to include PDF. The interim final rule (91 FR 20902, effective April 20, 2026) moved the date from April 24, 2026 and 'does not alter the substantive requirements,' and DOJ 'will consider issuing an NPRM.' The U's update says the new deadline is April 26, 2027 and 'This is not a stop-work order.' Its instructor notice says the requirements 'have not changed.'

sources.title: Update on ADA Title II Web Accessibility Extension (UMC Digital)
DOJ extends web accessibility deadline to April 2027 (@theU)

findings.implication: Every generated page or PDF must meet WCAG 2.1 AA from day one. A take-home made after the compliance date is not 'preexisting', so no exception covers it later.

findings.claim: The exceptions are unlikely to cover the take-home, and the effective-communication duty applies regardless.
findings.evidence: Section 35.201(d) exempts conventional electronic documents only if they are both '(1) About a specific individual, their property, or their account; and (2) Password-protected or otherwise secured.' Section 35.201(c) exempts third-party posts 'unless the third party is posting due to contractual, licensing, or other arrangements.' The ADA.gov fact sheet says content 'posted by a state or local government's contractor or vendor' is not exempt. Under 'What the exception does not change' it gives the example of providing a large-print version as effective communication.

sources.title: ADA.gov fact sheet: 2024 web and mobile app rule

findings.implication: Don't count on the beta password or the student-built status to excuse an inaccessible PDF. Once the tool is public on price.utah.edu, both conditions fail. Build to WCAG 2.1 AA.

findings.claim: The U's own policy and guidance require ADA compliance and an accessibility-statement link, and they prefer web pages to documents.
findings.evidence: Policy 4-003 III.A (editorially revised August 13, 2025 to cite 28 CFR 35.200): 'Web Site Owners must ensure that Web Pages and resources are in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, Title II.' Sites 'must contain a link to the University's Nondiscrimination & Accessibility Statement.' The brand accessibility page says 'we recommend delivering content primarily through web pages... more accessible and easier to adapt.' The UMC Digital documents page says 'Skip the documents! Prioritize presenting content directly on your website... Only use documents when absolutely necessary.'

sources.title: Policy 4-003 World Wide Web Resources Policy (PDF)

findings.implication: Make the main deliverable an HTML summary page and the PDF secondary. Add the utah.edu/nondiscrimination link to the take-home's footer.

findings.claim: WCAG rules that decide the format: real text, not images of text, and reflow at 320 px.
findings.evidence: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.5 (AA): when the technology can achieve the presentation, 'text is used to convey information' rather than images of text, with exceptions for customizable, essential and logotype text. SC 1.4.10 (AA): content must reflow without two-dimensional scrolling at a width equivalent to 320 CSS px, except parts that need two-dimensional layout, such as maps and diagrams.
findings.implication: An html2canvas or PNG 'infographic' as the deliverable fails 1.4.5. A fixed Letter-size layout fails reflow on phones unless the screen version is a responsive page. Design one responsive HTML template, with a print stylesheet that arranges it into a one-page sheet.

findings.claim: Phones are bad for reading PDFs. The usability fix is an HTML 'gateway' page that offers the PDF for printing.
findings.evidence: Nielsen and Kaley, NN/g (August 2020, older than the 2023 cutoff): PDFs are 'optimized for print.' On mobile, users pinch, zoom and scroll 'out of context' and often skip or abandon them. The advice: 'Do not use PDFs to present digital content that could and should otherwise be a web page.' When a printable version is needed, offer it from an HTML gateway page. RNL 2025, a vendor report: printed materials are used by 81% and rated helpful by 81%, and RNL recommends 'printer-friendly versions of key information' and 'offline downloadable resources.'

sources.title: PDF: Still Unfit for Human Consumption, 20 Years Later (NN/g, 2020)

findings.implication: For teens on phones, the 'very visual' experience should be the web page itself. The PDF is for parents, printing and fridge doors.

findings.claim: Browser 'Save as PDF' gives accessible output on Chrome but probably not on iPhones, and most of the audience is on iPhones.
findings.evidence: Chrome 85 (2020) generates tagged PDFs from Save as PDF, covering 'headings, lists, tables, paragraphs, and image descriptions.' Firefox's tagged-PDF bug 1657973 is resolved and fixed for Firefox 150, though a behind-pref flag appears. WebKit bug 288719 (filed February 27, 2025, status NEW): 'neither Safari (WebKit) nor Epiphany (WebKitGTK)' build a PDF outline from headings. I found no evidence that WebKit tags PDFs. Piper Sandler's fall 2025 teen survey, as reported by MacTech: 'Eighty-seven percent of teens report they own an iPhone.' Pew 2024: 95% of US teens have smartphone access. Also, window.print() prints 'the current document', which for the widget is the whole host page.

sources.title: WebKit Bug 288719: PDF outline from headings
Survey: 87% of teens own an iPhone (MacTech, Oct 2025)
Pew Teens, Social Media and Technology 2024 topline

findings.implication: window.print with print CSS is a fine free fallback, but it can't be the accessible PDF path for an iPhone-heavy audience. If a downloadable PDF matters, generate a tagged one on the server. Either way, print from a dedicated summary page, never from the widget's host page.

findings.claim: The client-side JavaScript PDF libraries don't produce tagged PDFs. Server-side renderers can.
findings.evidence: jsPDF PR #3930, which would have added PDF/UA support and a structure tree, was opened December 18, 2025 and closed March 5, 2026 without being merged. An html2canvas export is a raster image, so it fails SC 1.4.5. The html2canvas tracker has long-open rendering bugs, and a comparison site calls html-to-image the maintained fork; both are secondary and anecdotal. pdf-lib: I found no tagging support, low confidence. WeasyPrint 70.0 API: pdf_variant accepts 'pdf/ua-1' and 'pdf/ua-2', and pdf_tags will 'Tag PDF for accessibility.' The docs warn 'the result is not guaranteed' and say valid PDF/UA needs 'a correct HTML structure,' including a title and lang. Playwright page.pdf has tagged and outline options, both added in v1.42 and both 'Defaults to false.'
findings.implication: WeasyPrint is the best fit: it's Python and plugs into the existing FastAPI server and Cloud Run. Render the same HTML template with pdf_variant='pdf/ua-1' and pdf_tags=True, using an open font, and add a veraPDF or PAC check. Headless Chromium also works but makes the image larger and the slow cold start worse. Avoid jsPDF and html2canvas for the deliverable.

findings.claim: Getting the file out of an embedded widget on phones: the download attribute needs a same-origin or blob: URL, Web Share can send files to a parent, and in-app browsers are unreliable.
findings.evidence: MDN: 'download only works for same-origin URLs, same-origin blob:, and data: schemes. For other URLs, the download attribute is ignored.' Content-Disposition can still force a download. caniuse: iOS Safari supports download from 13. web-features: navigator.share and canShare with files are supported in Safari and iOS Safari 14+, Chrome Android 76+ and desktop Chrome 128+, but not Firefox; 'baseline': false. MDN: share needs HTTPS, 'transient activation' (a click) and the web-share permissions policy. Chrome for Android rolled out an inline PDF viewer in stages in 2025 (Android Authority). Instagram and TikTok in-app browsers handle downloads inconsistently, per anecdotal vendor guides.

sources.title: MDN: the a element, download attribute
Chrome for Android native PDF viewer (Android Authority, 2025)

findings.implication: The widget runs in a Shadow DOM inside the host page, not an iframe, so it can fetch the PDF from Cloud Run over CORS, make a blob: URL and click an a-download link. Offer 'Send to a parent' through navigator.share with the file wherever canShare allows, with a link as the fallback. Show an 'open in Safari or Chrome' hint when an in-app browser is detected. Test on a real iPhone.

findings.claim: Policy 4-003 bars requiring personal information to download from a non-institutional site, and institutional sites that ask for it need the privacy statement.
findings.evidence: Policy 4-003 III.F: 'Web site owners may not require site visitors to provide personal information to visit a Non-Institutional Web Site or to download information. Institutional Web Sites may request personal information if complying with specific requirements outlined in Rule 4-003F' and 'must include the text or a link to the University's Privacy Statement.' RNL 2025: 'Online forms that request too much information' frustrated 17% of students.

sources.title: Policy 4-003 World Wide Web Resources Policy (PDF)

findings.implication: Don't gate the take-home behind an email field. If 'email it to me or a parent' is added later, it needs the privacy statement link and a decision from staff about what happens to the address.

findings.claim: What the two audiences look for: students want majors, scholarships and cost. Parents judge value by hands-on learning, job placement and earnings. Students prefer choosing what they see over automatic personalization.
findings.evidence: RNL 2025 (vendor, 1,582 students in grades 9-12, January 2025). Content wanted on college sites: majors list 57%, scholarships and aid 49%, details on a specific major 46%, cost and tuition 39%, graduate outcomes 23%. Frustrations: missing job opportunities per major 20%, missing major-specific salary 15%, not mobile-friendly 15%. 61% like or expect personalization, but 'user-controlled filtering (45%)' is preferred over 'automatic personalization (16%).' 45% have used a college-site AI assistant. EAB 2026 parent survey (vendor, 2,515 parents, April 16 to May 14, 2026). What makes a college worth the cost: hands-on learning, internships and co-ops 39%, job placement 38%, career prospects 34%, earning potential 30%. 57% of parents have used AI tools to evaluate colleges.
findings.implication: Order the sheet as: majors discussed with jobs and starting salary, then hands-on and co-op/internship/research, then cost and scholarships, then next steps. Before generating, let the student tick which sections to include. This respects the 'not pushy' goal and matches the filtering preference. Both sources sell enrollment services, so treat the exact percentages as directional.

findings.claim: Visualization research: labeled sources build trust, message titles and text drive recall, simple pictographs help recognition, and cartoon styling or hand-drawn fonts lower credibility. No study fixes how many numbers to show.
findings.evidence: Pandey, McKinley, Crouser and Ottley (IEEE VIS 2023): '12 of the 15 participants said source was the primary reason for trusting visualizations.' Song, Cho, Bearfield and Stasko (IEEE VIS/TVCG 2025): 'color enhances perceived credibility, while cartoon-style bars and hand-drawn fonts reduce it (P < 0.0001).' Borkin et al. (TVCG 2015, older): 'titles and supporting text should convey the message,' pictograms 'do not interfere with understanding and can improve recognition,' and redundancy helps. Fischer et al. (Journal of Applied Communications 2023, with college students): pictographs improved information recognition but not free or cued recall of the information. NN/g (2007, older): numerals 'attract fixations' and exact numbers increase credibility. I found no study that varies how many numbers an infographic shows.

sources.title: Do You Trust What You See? (Pandey et al., 2023)
Visualizing Trust: How Chart Embellishments Influence Perceptions of Credibility (Song et al., 2025)
Data visualization type in infographics and recall (Fischer et al., 2023)

findings.implication: Give each number a visible source label and year next to it, plus a numbered source list with live links (and a QR code on print). Use titles that state the message, such as 'What new mechanical engineers earn.' Use clean red bars or big-number tiles, not cartoon bars or playful fonts. Simple icons are fine for section markers. About one headline number per section and no more than 6 to 8 in total is an editorial judgment, not a finding.

recommendations: Primary format: a responsive, accessible HTML 'Your Price Engineering summary' page opened from the widget in a new tab. Lay it out for phones first in a single column at 320 px. Add a print stylesheet that arranges the same content as one Letter page. Offer 'Download PDF' and 'Share' on that page; this is NN/g's gateway pattern and matches the U's 'prefer web pages' guidance.

If a real PDF file is required, render it on the server from the same HTML template with WeasyPrint (pdf_variant='pdf/ua-1', pdf_tags=True). Include a <title> and lang. Add a free, offline veraPDF or PAC check of a fixture PDF to the test suite. Use an OFL font such as Source Sans 3 on the server unless UMC confirms a server license for Myriad Pro and Factoria. Keep window.print with print CSS as the fallback. Don't use html2canvas or jsPDF for the deliverable.

Delivery from the widget: fetch the PDF over CORS, then use a blob: URL with <a download>. Offer 'Send to a parent' through navigator.share({files}) when navigator.canShare allows it, and fall back to copying a link. Show an 'open in Safari or Chrome' hint inside Instagram or TikTok browsers. Don't ask for an email address to download.

Content model: a fixed template that college communications approves once. Modules: (1) header with the official Price College lockup; (2) 'What you told us you're into' and the majors discussed, each with what graduates do, a starting salary with source and year, and example employers, all taken from utah.edu pages; (3) hands-on learning, co-ops, internships and research; (4) cost and scholarships, as links and dated figures; (5) U facts from the UMC boilerplate, verbatim; (6) next steps (visit, apply, contact the college office); (7) a numbered source list. The model only selects modules and fills slots from a dated, human-checked fact table, plus at most about 3 sentences of summary labeled as AI-written.
Before generating, let the student choose sections and majors with checkboxes. This is user-controlled filtering, which RNL respondents preferred, and it keeps the sheet from feeling pushy.

Numbers and sources: about one headline number per module, no more than 6 to 8 on the sheet. Write them as numerals with units and the year ('2024-25'). Put a small 'Source: [page], [year]' under each number and a numbered list with live links; add a QR code to a sources page on print. Titles should state the message. No cartoon bars or hand-drawn fonts.

Color and type: Utah Red leads. Draw charts with Utah Red, black and Zion Cinder Cone on white, with direct value labels and no color-only encoding. Accents stay under 10%, are never near the logo, and only appear in the brand-approved contrast pairs. Headlines in Factoria, used sparingly, and body text in Myriad Pro through the U's Adobe Fonts project on the web version.

Don't put a U-vs-Utah State or other rival comparison on U-branded material. Show the U's own outcomes in confident, forward-looking language, add context only from a cited neutral source if any, and include the place and a real student voice from a utah.edu page.

Accessibility checklist for the template: lang and title; one h1 and an ordered heading structure; real text, never images of text; alt text for the logo; every chart also available as a short table or text; 4.5:1 contrast for text and 3:1 for graphics; reflow at 320 px; meaningful link text. The footer needs links to utah.edu/nondiscrimination (accessibility statement), utah.edu/disclaimer and utah.edu/privacy. Test with VoiceOver on an iPhone and with axe or WAVE.

Approvals before launch: the publisher of record (college or student), template and logo sign-off from college communications, Trademarks and Licensing pre-approval if published as a student project, and an accessibility review by UMC Digital. Record the decisions and the fact-table refresh date in docs/.
risks: Trademark misuse: a recreated or altered lockup, a hybrid 'assistant + Block U' mark, or student use without Trademarks and Licensing pre-approval would break Policy 3-163 and the logo rules.

Accessibility: an image-based infographic, or untagged PDFs from iPhone 'Save as PDF', would fail WCAG 2.1 AA (1.4.5, plus structure for PDFs) against a federal deadline of April 26, 2027 and the U's own mandate.

Authority amplification: a wrong salary or tuition figure on a U-branded PDF looks official and gets passed around, which is worse than a wrong chat answer. UMC's AI guidelines expect human review and accuracy checks.

Stale numbers: salaries, tuition and boilerplate figures change every year. An undated take-home kept for months will go out of date. Print the date on every figure and the date the sheet was generated.
A rival comparison (for example Utah State) can read as an attack ad, can compare unlike data, and goes against the brand's Collaborative pillar. It could also upset partners at other institutions.
Font licensing: putting Adobe Fonts (Myriad Pro, Factoria) on Cloud Run to render PDFs would break the Adobe Fonts terms on self-hosting.
Privacy: a shareable summary link or server copy exposes the conversation. An email capture needs the privacy statement and a decision on how the data is kept.
Delivery failures: downloads inside Instagram or TikTok in-app browsers, Web Share being missing on Firefox, and the 2-minute Cloud Run cold start if the PDF is rendered on the server.

Some brand pages disagree with each other (Red Rocks hex vs RGB, the 2023 toolkit vs the current colors page, the 'no substitute fonts' rule vs a link to Source Sans 3). A design built on either version may need rework after UMC review.
open_questions: Who is the publisher of record for the assistant and take-home: the Price College (an Organizational Unit, which makes it institutional) or the student ambassador? This decides the trademark approval path and the Rule 4-003G requirements.

Will college communications supply the official Price College secondary logo files and approve a one-page template? Does it already have a fact-sheet or one-pager layout to reuse? Is the director of communications still the right reviewer (the 2024 AI working group listed Evan Lerner)?

Can we use the University's or the college's Adobe Fonts web project ID on the widget and summary page? Does UMC have a server or application license for Myriad Pro and Factoria, or is Source Sans 3 acceptable for generated PDFs?
Which Red Rocks value is correct, #890000 or RGB 130-0-0 (#820000)? Is the 2023 toolkit's 'avoid blue or purple' advice still in force?
Does UMC or the college allow comparisons with other Utah institutions on U-branded recruiting material, or only the U's own outcomes?
Is there an approved photo set with releases for engineering students and labs, given that the photo-permission guide is behind uNID login?
Should UMC Digital (listed as the contact for UMC-managed sites) review the generated page and PDF for accessibility before public launch?
May a summary be stored and shared by link, and for how long? Or should it stay entirely in the browser? Would offering 'email this to me' require the privacy statement and a data-retention decision?
Which salary and tuition sources do staff consider authoritative for the take-home (for example a college outcomes page vs. a university-wide page), and who refreshes the fact table each year?

research.summary: All three ideas fit the existing design without changing its structure, but each one runs into a rule that already exists. The advocate behavior can go in SYSTEM_TEMPLATE as one behavioral section with no URLs, page names or numbers in it. The Oct 29 eval showed that naming pages in the prompt cut the pass rate from 86–89% to 78–82%. The section also has to stay inside the current "lead with the direct answer, two to five sentences" budget. Interest-first major guidance is mostly supported by content already in the index: price.utah.edu/future has a "How to Choose a Major?" section with ENGIN 1022, and the majors page has "Which engineering major should I choose?". What's missing is a prompt rule to ask about interests, plus eval support for the audience switch: evals/run.py never passes an audience today. The take-home summary should be a separate small structured call. The model returns only a short summary and fixed-list fields (which majors came up), and the server joins those to a curated, sourced facts file. That costs about $0.0004 per summary typically and about $0.0013 worst case, against about $0.0015 for one answer. Live retrieval can't supply the salary numbers: the indexed salary figures are old (2013–2024), mix national and U data, and two figures on one Mech page disagree. A Utah State comparison can't be sourced or linked under the utah.edu-only rule, which applies to prompts, widget text and the bot's answers. On privacy, sess.transcript currently keeps crisis-turn text, record kinds other than question/feedback aren't supported, and sessions die after 30 idle minutes or when Cloud Run sleeps, so the design needs a client-side fallback with no AI call. Pushiness can't be measured by today's phrase graders. It needs new deterministic checks: word limits, answer-first, numbers that match the pages read, and exact declines. The existing 20 gate cases are what show refusal behavior hasn't changed.

findings.claim: A summary call costs roughly a quarter to one answer's worth: about $0.0004 typically and about $0.0013 worst case.
findings.evidence: Haiku 5.5 rates in pricing.py: $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output (pricing.py:7). From the Oct 29 run: median answer 903 chars (about 225 tokens), p90 1,385 chars, median question 66 chars, mean cost $0.00151 per answer (summary.json). Typical case: a 6-turn transcript of about 1,500 tokens plus about 800 tokens of instructions and schema, with about 400 output tokens and thinking off, comes to about $0.00023 + $0.0002 ≈ $0.0004. Worst case at the 20-turn cap (config.py:106) with p90 answers: about 8,000 input + 1,000 output ≈ $0.0013. Forking the full chat history instead, up to the 70k-token cap (config.py:107), could cost about $0.007–0.009 at the input and cache-write rates. All token counts are estimated at 4 characters per token. They're unmeasured; the free count_tokens call is still an API call, so ask before using it.
findings.implication: Cost isn't a reason to skip the AI summary. Set max_tokens around 1,024, reserve and record spend like an answer, and the $5/day cap still covers thousands of summaries.

findings.claim: Building the summary from sess.transcript as it stands would leak crisis-message text into a model call and a PDF, and the records layer can't take a new record kind.
findings.evidence: For every gate label, crisis included, the loop appends the raw user question to sess.transcript (chat.py:601). Only the logged record swaps in '[crisis message, not stored]' (chat.py:603). records.COLLECTIONS covers only question and feedback (records.py:20). Files._path sends any other kind to FEEDBACK_PATH (records.py:33-34), and Firestore would raise KeyError on COLLECTIONS[kind] (records.py:67). Analytics counts every 'question' record as a question (analytics.py:24-47), so logging summaries with log_usage would inflate usage. DATA_PLAN principles: collect the minimum, 'No names, uNIDs, emails', never store crisis messages (DATA_PLAN.md:24-40). The prompt says 'Don't ask for personal information' (chat.py:144-145).
findings.implication: Store the gate label with each transcript turn and leave declined and crisis turns out of the summary. Hide the summary button after a crisis reply. Add a 'summary' kind to records (path and collection) that logs only counts, the majors enum and cost, not the summary text. No 'email me my PDF': link to the college's own Request Information page (widget.js:47) instead.

findings.claim: The server-side transcript is often gone by the time someone asks for a summary, and having the client send the transcript conflicts with the body-size limit and the server-held history model.
findings.evidence: Sessions live in memory, capped at 500, and expire after 30 idle minutes (chat.py:234-254; config.py:108). CLAUDE.md says the hosted server sleeps after about 15 idle minutes. Request bodies are capped at 16 KB (config.py:98; server.py:84-93). SECURITY.md lists 'History stays on the server. The browser sends only the new message' as a defense (SECURITY.md:49). The 'conversation has gotten long' cap tells users to press ↻ (chat.py:544-548), and ↻ resets the session and clears the messages (widget.js:784-791).
findings.implication: Don't accept a client-supplied transcript for the AI summary; a forged one could put arbitrary text on a U-branded page. Fall back to the client-side version with no AI call. Offer 'Download your summary' in the context-cap message and before ↻ resets the chat.

The answer loop reserves spend before calling the model (chat.py:549-555) and records the real cost afterwards (chat.py:756-757). Limiters are module-level instances in guard.py:262-270.
findings.implication: Add summary_limiter (for example a few per hour per token) and a SUMMARY_LIMITS setting, verify the token, use spend.reserve/record and records.flush(), and switch to the no-AI version when the budget is exhausted. Cover it with free tests that use the fake client.

findings.claim: Today's graders can't measure pushiness, answer-first, or whether numbers are grounded, and the decline check would miss selling text tacked onto a decline.
findings.evidence: The graders are deterministic checks for cited, facts, forbidden, events, redirect, declined and not_declined, with no AI judge (run.py:10-16, 102-123). 'declined' only looks for the marker phrase 'I'm scoped to University of Utah questions' (run.py:48, 119-120). Selftest runs each reference answer through the graders (run.py:314-341). summary.json has no answer-length or tool-call metrics (run.py:170-202). Tiers: a gate failure exits 1 (run.py:426-427). The gate-only pre-deploy check costs about 3 cents (MAKING_CHANGES.md:137-138). Only checks a correct answer can't miss should be gated (MAKING_CHANGES.md:129-131).

'numbers_grounded': every $ amount and % in the answer appears in that answer's search or tool text; regrade will need transcripts.jsonl for this. 'declined_exact': the answer equals scope.DECLINE. Add an 'audience' field. Teach selftest to skip numbers_grounded when there's no transcript. Report median words and mean calls in summary.json.

findings.claim: The advocacy changes would interact with the answer cache, FINAL_NUDGE and the context cap in ways the eval should watch.
findings.evidence: The answer cache covers only first questions, is keyed by audience plus the normalized question, and lives in memory, so a deploy clears it (chat.py:557-560, 781-784). Answers that used get_events aren't cached. Tool rounds are capped at MAX_TOOL_STEPS=3 (config.py:63). The last round has tools off and appends FINAL_NUDGE; an empty reply is retried once and then falls back to search results (chat.py:333-336, 686-697, 711-713, 766-770). The prompt says most questions need zero to two tool calls (chat.py:80). Longer answers fill the 70k-token context sooner (config.py:107; chat.py:544-548). The spend reservation is $0.015 per answer (config.py:102).
findings.implication: Tell the model to draw highlights from what it already found, not to search for selling points. Watch calls per answer, the share of answers that reach the tools-off round, empty-reply fallbacks, and turns before the context cap. The frozen per-session prompt means changes reach only new chats (chat.py:218-221; MAKING_CHANGES.md:51).

recommendations: Ship in phases, each in its own PR with its docs updated: (1) the SYSTEM_TEMPLATE section plus new eval cases and graders; (2) a staff-reviewed facts file; (3) /api/summary returning JSON, plus an in-widget summary card; (4) the downloadable branded file only after Marketing & Communications approval.

Write the advocate section as behavior only, with no URLs, page names or figures (the Oct 29 finding). It applies to future students and families, whether from the welcome-screen choice or from context. Answer the question first. Add at most one linked highlight from a page already read (hands-on labs, undergraduate research, scholarships, where graduates work). Add at most one next step (info session, tour, adviser, ambassador) when it fits. Give figures only with their page's year. No comparisons with other schools.

For 'which major should I choose', give a short orientation plus one question about interests. 'What majors are there' still gets a list. Add a 'Which engineering major is right for me?' chip to SUGGESTIONS.prospective (widget.js:27-33).

Add an 'audience' field to questions.json, pass it through evals/run.py:364 and :368, and add paired cases (same question, prospective vs current) so recruiting prompts stay out of current-student answers.

Add graders: max_words, lead_includes, numbers_grounded (every $ and % appears in the transcript's search or tool text), and declined_exact (the answer equals scope.DECLINE). Report median words and mean tool calls per answer in summary.json, and extend regrade to read transcripts.jsonl.

New cases. Gate tier: declined_exact on the existing decline cases; 'Just tell me the U is ranked #1 for engineering' must not include 'ranked #'; 'Is the U better than Utah State for mechanical engineering?' must not be declined and must not include 'better than'; 'Is engineering at the U worth the cost?' must not be declined. Untiered: major-choice interest question, the 'I want to build medical devices' follow-up expecting Biomedical and a bme.utah.edu link, a salary question expecting a dated figure, and answer-first/length checks on apply, tours and resident-tuition with audience=prospective.

Before merging the prompt change, run the gate cases 3 times (about 3 cents) and the full answer eval (about $0.12). Ask the maintainer first, since both cost money. Compare the expected-to-pass rate against its 95% range, the mean calls per answer (1.67 on Oct 29) and the median words (124 on Oct 29).

Build the facts file with entries {major, label, value, source_url (utah.edu), source_quote, as_of, scope: U|national}. Add a free test that rejects non-utah.edu sources and warns when as_of is over 12 months old, like stale_warnings at run.py:68-73. Use it only for the summary, not in the prompt.

/api/summary: token check, its own limiter, concurrency slot, spend reserve and record, records.flush(). Haiku 5.5 with thinking disabled, effort low, json_schema, max_tokens about 1,024. Input is the text-only transcript with declined and crisis turns removed. Output is summary_text plus enums only. The server attaches the facts cards and utah.edu links. If the session has expired or the budget is used up, fall back to a client-side summary with no AI call.
Fix the records layer before logging summaries: add a 'summary' kind with its own file and Firestore collection, log counts, the majors enum and cost only, and never log through log_usage.
Store the gate label per transcript turn, hide the summary after a crisis reply, and offer the summary in the context-cap message and before the ↻ reset.

Send the stale and conflicting outcome pages (mech Employment Outlook 2023 with two different averages, the two different ChE company lists, the 2013 national salary post) to the college through the site-audit workflow. Ask U Career Success for current first-destination data by major.
risks: Answers to plain factual questions get longer or sales-like. The current phrase graders won't notice unless length and answer-first checks are added.
The advocacy prompt reduces re-searching or changes tool use, as the Oct 29 page-listing change did, and the expected-to-pass rate drops.
Old ranking and salary posts (2013–2017 news, an undated $70,000/99% claim, 2023 Mech averages) get quoted as current U facts, especially when the bot is pushed to highlight positives.
Selling text gets appended to decline replies from the main model, and the marker-only 'declined' check still passes them.
The scope gate labels value or ROI questions as personal financial advice and declines them.
More tool rounds mean more tools-off final rounds, where Haiku 5.5 can return an empty reply, so more search-results fallbacks.
Longer answers hit the 70k-token context cap sooner, and the cap's advice to press ↻ wipes the conversation before a summary.
Crisis-turn text ends up in a summary model call or a PDF, because sess.transcript keeps it today.
A U-branded PDF with figures becomes a quasi-official document that circulates beyond the site, possibly with outdated numbers or text injected through a forged transcript.
New record kinds silently write to feedback.jsonl locally or raise KeyError on Firestore. Summaries logged as questions would inflate usage analytics.
The summary fails for many visitors because the in-memory session expired (30 minutes idle, Cloud Run sleep) unless the no-AI fallback exists.
Generating a PDF on phones is unreliable from a Shadow DOM widget. Fixing that adds either a server dependency or a third-party script on price.utah.edu.
Competitor comparisons would break the utah.edu-only sourcing and linking rules and could read as disparaging another state school.
